Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

claim verb

demand as one’s own or one’s due

also lay claim to, claim back, claim the credit, claim one’s share

classical

Cic. Arch. 19: Chiī suum vindicant
Plin. Ep. 6.32.2: partem oneris tuī mihi vindicō
Traupman 291: vindicāre, claim as one’s own

vindicō, vindicāre, vindicāvī, vindicātum

verb, first conjugation; often with sibi

claim (as one’s own)

Lewis & Short: “to lay claim to as one’s own”; sibi vindicāre, to claim for oneself (a share, credit, a right).

Other words

  • postulō, postulāre, postulāvī, postulātum — claim, demand (what one is owed)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 201: suum jūs postulat; Traupman 291: postulāre, claim (demand)

  • repetō, repetere, repetīvī, repetītum — claim back, ask for the return of

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 19: Salamīniī repetunt

  • arrogō (adrogō), arrogāre, arrogāvī, arrogātum — claim (for oneself) what is not one’s due

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 292 (Lewis & Short): sapientiam sibi adrogāre

Examples

  • Homērum Colophōniī cīvem esse dīcunt suum, Chiī suum vindicant, Salamīniī repetunt, Smyrnaeī vērō suum esse cōnfirmant

    The people of Colophon say that Homer was their citizen, the Chians claim him as theirs, the Salaminians claim him back, and the people of Smyrna insist that he is theirsCic. Arch. 19

  • Vērum enim, quandō bene prōmeruit, fīat: suum jūs postulat.

    Well, since he’s earned it, so be it: he’s claiming what is his by right.Ter. Ad. 201

See also claim.
